title: How many independent control channels does an addressable skin need?
kind: simulation (pigment-actuator array + observer blur + projected-gradient controller)
headline: At the measured motor-unit size of nine actuators per channel, the knee is 579 +/- 0 channels over a 4 x 4 mm patch carrying 3904 actuators - about 36 channels per mm^2, or one channel per 6.7 actuators. Across unit sizes the knee tracks the number needed to COVER the array (K/m) within a factor of 1.00-5.41, so for everything but the finest target the channel budget is set by innervating the skin at all, not by the complexity of the pattern. The real animal is not a free parameter here: Renard et al. 2026 resolved 754 putative motor units driving 1829 chromatophores, which is 0.412 channels per actuator and motor units of about nine, so on this patch the animal sits at 1609 channels - PAST the knee on every target, reaching 99-101% of the fidelity it would get from one channel per chromatophore.

preregistration.primary_metric: variance explained (R^2) on the observer-blurred reflectance field, clipped below at 0; the target is affinely mapped into the skin's own achievable range first, so the metric scores pattern fidelity and not the pigment layer's contrast range
secondary_metrics: mean absolute error of the blurred field
unclipped R^2, reported as a diagnostic

knee_rules.knee_95: smallest N whose R^2 reaches 0.95 x R^2 at N = K
knee_rules.knee_curvature: maximum vertical distance from the chord of the (log10 N, R^2) curve

preregistration.note: Declared in the module docstring of code/control_channels.py before the first run. No target was added, dropped or re-parameterised afterwards. The two uniform targets have zero variance, so R^2 is undefined for them and is returned as null rather than as 1.0 - a score of 1 earned by an empty denominator would otherwise have been averaged in with real ones.

model.description: Actuators placed by Poisson-disc sampling at the measured chromatophore density on a square skin patch, each expanding from a retracted to an expanded disc area in the measured ratio. N channels each drive a motor unit of m actuators; an actuator's drive is the clamped sum over the channels that own it. The pigment area field is blurred by an observer point-spread function and converted to reflectance through a random-overlap coverage law. Channel activations are optimised by Adam with box projection.
state_variables: per-actuator drive u = clamp(sum of owning channels)
equations: S = G * (sum_i A_i delta_i) / pixel area
R^2 = 1 - SSE / SST on the blurred field

parameters.name: actuator_density
parameters.source: Mean chromatophore density measured on cuttlefish dorsal mantle: 2.44e-4 per um^2 (the paper's own simulation reproduced it at 2.52e-4 +/- 0.1e-4). Reiter S et al. (Laurent G) 2018, Nature 562:361-366, PMID 30333578 (read: full text).

parameters.name: area_ratio
parameters.source: +155.06% mean surface-area increase on expansion. Hadjisolomou SP et al. 2021, Front Physiol 12:675252, PMID 34220538 (read: full text). A startle response, not a measured maximum - see the actuator study.

parameters.name: unit_sizes
parameters.source: Spans the measured range from two independent studies: motor units of 2-10 chromatophores with a median motor ELEMENT of 3 (Reiter S et al. (Laurent G) 2018, Nature 562:361-366, PMID 30333578 (read: full text)); a mean of about 9 chromatophores per putative motor unit, 90% under 14 and occasionally up to 30 (Renard MDM et al. 2026, eLife 110074, PMID 42418335 (read: full text)). The value 1 is included as the one-channel-per-actuator limit, which no animal has.

parameters.name: within_unit_nnd_um
parameters.source: Mean within-cluster nearest-neighbour distance 40.548 +/- 46.946 um, against a global array NND of 6.130 +/- 1.589 um: chromatophores in one motor unit are NOT immediate neighbours. Renard MDM et al. 2026, eLife 110074, PMID 42418335 (read: full text).

parameters.name: coverage_full
parameters.source: Areal coverage with every actuator expanded. Not measured. The resulting expanded diameter is 99.5 um, which lands at the top of the measured 15-100 um chromatophore diameter range - a weak corroboration, not a source.

parameters.name: r_pigment
parameters.source: Reflectance of fully pigmented skin. Not measured; the declared metric maps the target into the skin's own range, so this sets contrast and not pattern fidelity.

parameters.name: r_background
parameters.source: Reflectance of the unpigmented backing. Not measured.

parameters.name: blur_in_spacings
parameters.source: Observer point-spread sigma. NO predator acuity number was sourced. Expressed in units of actuator spacing so the result is at least scale-free in the array.

parameters.name: patch_mm
parameters.source: Edge of the square modelled skin patch.

parameters.name: grid
parameters.source: Raster on which the field is scored.

parameters.name: knee_fraction
parameters.source: Declared before the sweep: the knee is the smallest N reaching this fraction of the score at one channel per actuator.

parameters.name: seeds
parameters.source: Array seeds. Every headline number is reported with its spread across these, not as a single value.

model.parameter_note: `sourced` means the number appears in a paper we read, measured in the thing being modelled. A value measured in another tissue or another species is `assumed`, with the proxy named in `source`.

sweep.where: Nebius job aijob-e00mz387dqe1bm2y5x, gpu-h100-sxm preset 1gpu-16vcpu-200gb, python:3.12-slim, 16 worker processes. Pure NumPy; the GPU preset was the only way to get 16 cores.

headline.why_the_spread_is_zero: The s.d. across seeds and targets is 0.0, and that is a GRID ARTEFACT, not a precision claim. The channel count is swept on a 14-point logarithmic grid, so a knee can only ever land on a grid point; every seed and every non-trivial target happened to land on the same one. The real uncertainty is therefore bounded below by the grid spacing, which here is a factor of about 1.9 in either direction - the neighbouring grid points are 306 and 1094. Quote the knee as 'between 306 and 1094, nearest grid point 579', not as '579 +/- 0'. A finer grid would be needed to say more, and the agreement across 30 independent runs is evidence that the knee is stable to within one grid step, which is a weaker and true statement.
headline.statistic_note: The pre-registration defines the knee on the MEAN curve, which gives one number per target and no spread. Both are reported: `knee95_of_mean_curves_*` is the declared statistic, and `knee95_mean_channels` with its s.d. is the distribution of per-seed knees, which is what a spec sheet needs. They are computed from the same runs and should agree closely; if they do not, the per-seed distribution is skewed and the mean-curve number is the one to quote.

knee_is_set_by_coverage_not_complexity.test: If the channel budget were set by the pattern's spatial detail, the knee would depend on the target and not on the unit size. If it is set by covering the array, the knee should sit near K/m. Both are computed below.

where_the_real_animal_sits.verdict: PAST the knee on every target

measured_operating_point.source: Renard MDM et al. 2026, eLife 110074, PMID 42418335 (read: full text via PMC). Species: Euprymna berryi and Sepia officinalis.
measured_operating_point.self_consistency: The paper's numbers close on themselves, which is why they can be used as an operating point rather than quoted loosely: 6795 ICs over 1829 chromatophores is 3.715 per chromatophore, and 754 motor units at 9.003 ICs each is 6788 memberships, or 3.711 per chromatophore. One IC per chromatophore per motor unit, so a unit of 9 ICs is a unit of about 9 CHROMATOPHORES - which matches the discussion's 'typically around ten chromatophores' and '90% fewer than 14'.
measured_operating_point.preserved_disagreement: One internal inconsistency in the source is kept rather than smoothed: the convex-hull areas are reported with a median of 136,199.10 um^2 while '90% of clusters had a convex hull area smaller than 51,513.25 um^2'. Both cannot hold. Nothing here depends on the hull areas, so it is recorded and not resolved.

results.oracle_caveat: The oracle wiring relaxes TWO constraints, not one: it chooses its motor units after seeing the target, and it partitions the whole array into N clusters regardless of the unit size m, so every actuator is innervated even when N*m < K. It is therefore a loose upper bound and the gap to it should not be read as 'what better wiring would buy'. Found by looking at the rendered panels, not by a control.

controls_declared_but_NOT_REACHED.status: DECLARED AND NOT REACHED - this is a gap in verification, not a clean result
controls_declared_but_NOT_REACHED.what_happened: The Nebius job emitted its sweep before running its controls, by design: an earlier run had thrown away 11,200 completed cells when a NameError in the control step killed the process before anything was written, so `emit()` was changed to commit the expensive result first. That change saved this sweep. It also means the block that survived in the job log is tagged `sweep-only`: the controls block never printed, and the hackathon token expired before the job could be re-run. The five controls below were declared in the module docstring before the sweep ran and have NOT been run against this dataset.

limitations: THE HEADLINE'S '99-101% of saturation' IS MEASURED AGAINST THE ANIMAL'S OWN MOTOR-UNIT SIZE, NOT AGAINST A PERFECT MATCH, and read carelessly it says the animal is near-optimal when it does not. At the measured unit size of nine actuators the achievable ceiling differs sharply by target: edge 0.971, square 0.961, stripes_coarse 0.958, mottle 0.950, gravel_1f 0.897 and stripes_fine only 0.644 (compact wiring, mean over five seeds). NO CHANNEL COUNT MOVES THESE. They are ceilings, not slow approaches: the curves are flat from roughly the knee onward, and at one channel per actuator - 3,904 channels, more than twice what the animal has - stripes_fine is still 0.644. What the result says is that the animal has every channel its unit size can use, and that a unit of nine is already too coarse to render fine detail. That is the same constraint the coverage test shows from the other side, where knee / (K/m) rises to 5.41 at thirty actuators per unit. This page must not be read as claiming cephalopod skin reproduces fine patterns well; it claims the animal is not channel-limited.
Everything here is a model. No skin was built, and the only measured inputs are the actuator density, the expansion ratio and the motor-unit sizes.

The observer's acuity is ASSUMED and it is the parameter the knee is most likely to depend on. No predator acuity number was sourced, so the blur is expressed in units of mean actuator spacing. A sharper observer needs more channels; we do not know by how much for any real fish.

The coverage law under-estimates true coverage by up to 16% relative (`coverage_law_vs_exact_union`, which FAILS). Its sensitivity arm shows the knee does not move, but the absolute reflectances in this model are biased.

Motor units here are compact or overlapping groups of WHOLE actuators. The real system is finer than that: a chromatophore is driven by about four independent sources acting on contiguous angular sectors, so the real array has roughly four times as many addressable elements as this model gives it. That makes our channel counts a LOWER bound on what the animal has, and it is the single biggest structural simplification here.

Retraction is instantaneous in this model: it solves for a steady pattern and says nothing about how fast the skin can move between two of them. The actuator study is where timing lives, and it fails its control arm.

One colour class only. Real skin layers light and dark chromatophores with iridophores and leucophores beneath, and the measured motor units are 89% monochromatic, so a real controller has at least two interleaved arrays.
The array is flat, square and unstretched. A real one grows, and the developmental routes in routes.json are about exactly that.
